guidance.opening:
波士顿秋日的薄雾贴着窗玻璃。史蒂文·诺特的办公室里，煤气灯把一叠租约和一枚黄铜镇纸照得发亮。这位房东站在桌后，把一份旧房产卷宗拍平，袖口上沾着墨渍。

「我是史蒂文·诺特。我刚继承了城里那栋老宅——街坊叫它科比特宅。房客待不久。上一户叫马卡里奥的，出了祸事后搬走了，家里还有人进了疯人院。我需要人把这事查清楚，好让房子能再租出去。所以才让你进这间办公室。」

他抬眼打量来人，并未递出钥匙或钞票。

「先说说：你是谁？平时做什么营生？」
guidance.advice: 1920s Boston. Occupations to suggest from the list only: Journalist, Private Investigator, Lawyer, Librarian, Professor, Police Detective, Police Officer, Antiquarian, Author, Parapsychologist, Doctor of Medicine, Dilettante, Clergy. Useful skills/languages without numbers: Library Use, History, Law, Fast Talk, Persuade, Spot Hidden, Listen, Occult (as rumor-handling, not confirmed Mythos), Latin or Italian for records and immigrant tenants. Era kit: notepad, press card or calling cards, modest cash of the investigator’s own, overcoat, flashlight—do not invent scenario keys or Knott’s advance. Public involvement: a landlord seeking someone to look into why no one will stay in an inherited house and to restore its name; research at newspapers, Hall of Records, neighbors, or former tenants is the public premise, not a signed job yet. Optional ties (not facts): acquaintance of a Boston landlord, curiosity about local haunted-house talk, professional interest in tenancy disputes or asylums. Optional motivation questions: why answer a landlord’s summons; any Boston roots. Preserve uncertainty: wrongness is rumor; do not state supernatural causes. Do not force a profession.
guidance.handoff: The visitor is in Steven Knott’s Boston office. Knott has introduced himself as the landlord who inherited the Corbitt House, mentioned that tenants will not stay, that the Macarios left after a disaster with family in an asylum, and that he wants the place’s reputation cleared. He has asked who the visitor is and what work they do. Identity is not settled; no commission has been accepted and no keys, money, or clues have been given. Continue the identity conversation in Knott’s Office.
